terms.gloss: a two-pronged fork; a forked prop
evidence: Verg. G. 1.264: exacuunt aliī vallōs furcāsque bicornēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The big fork of the farm, and any forked pole or prop; the fork one eats with is its diminutive, furcilla.

phrases.latin: nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret
phrases.english: you may drive nature out with a pitchfork, she will still come running back

sources: Lewis & Short: furca
